solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Punters search distractedly for pickpocket

indicators.note: acting distractedly, the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Gamblers frantically hunting for the thief who picked their pockets at the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse-snatcher is a street thief who grabs bags, close kin to a pickpocket.

clue.text: Tenderloin like this is bathed in juice when flipped

indicators.note: being bathed in a liquid means being surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside the other
flipping turns the word for juice round so it reads backwards

parts.note: sap is plant juice
so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: fillet steak basted in its juices and turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: The psoas is the loin muscle which, in beef, is the cut sold as tenderloin or fillet.

clue.text: Chariot: race that involves this etc

indicators.note: the letters of race that are said to involve, or contain mixed up, the answer together with the letters of etc

explanation.surface: A chariot race featuring this sort of vehicle and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: RACE THAT 'involves' the answer ('this') plus E, T, C, all mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratha is a Hindu temple car or war chariot, a sense found in Chambers.

clue.text: Reel for denoting dramatically lyrical music

parts.note: to reel is to spin round
to can stand for for, as in 'the key for the door' or 'to the door'

explanation.surface: A Scottish reel tune chosen to represent dramatic, lyrical music.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinto describes a lyric operatic voice with a dramatic, forceful edge, and music written for it.

clue.text: Jock's artfully dextrous getting fish to rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: eels are fish

explanation.surface: A Scot cleverly skilful at making fish come up to the fly.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a crossword name for a Scot, so a Scots word is wanted; EELS 'to rise' in a down entry reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Slee is the Scots form of sly, meaning cunning or artfully skilful.

clue.text: Fervent until trapped by a girl

indicators.note: being trapped by something means being held inside it

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
to can mean until, as in 'nine to five'

explanation.surface: An ardent suitor held captive by a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Amatory means relating to love, and so passionate or ardent in feeling.

clue.text: Pooh accordingly delays bit of honey to the end

indicators.note: the delayed letter is put at the end of what remains
delaying a letter means taking it out of its place to come later

parts.note: thus means accordingly, therefore

indicators.note: a bit of the word honey is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of honey

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh, true to form, saves the honey till last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delays bit of honey' moves the H of THUS to the end: THUS becomes TUS + H.
explanation.definitionFit: Tush and pooh are both exclamations of impatient contempt or dismissal.

clue.text: Product of Tesco, it's added to and enlarges one like itself

definitions.text: it's added to and enlarges one like itself

indicators.note: a product of a word's letters is something made by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Something made by a supermarket that grows when combined with others of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Product of' rearranges TESCO; the definition describes a coset in group theory, where cosets of a subgroup combine to build the whole group.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a coset is a set formed by combining a subgroup with an element, joining others to fill out a larger group.

clue.text: Cheer up jumper overturned in ditch when one's thrown

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other
one is A, and throwing it out removes one A

parts.note: a ha-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a fence

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading upwards, backwards
overturned means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, is a jumper

explanation.surface: A kangaroo tumbling into a ditch prompts a cheer when someone is thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunk ditch bounding a park; when one's thrown it is HAH, and the jumper, up and overturned, is OOR, which goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoorah is a shout of joy or approval, a variant of hurrah.

clue.text: School book? Number left off study in the back

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: left off means omitted, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A schoolbook with a number missing from a study at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A reader is a textbook of passages used for teaching children to read.

clue.text: When coming from behind old horse breaks bone

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it
coming from behind means read from the back, so reversed

parts.note: as means when
capul is an old word for a horse

explanation.surface: An old horse coming up from behind breaks a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' coming from behind gives SA, and capul, an archaic or dialect word for a horse found in Chambers, breaks into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The scapula is the shoulder blade, a flat bone of the shoulder.

clue.text: Conservative, tho' with EU etc prepared for a bunk

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are worked into shape

explanation.surface: A Tory, though alongside the EU and so on, is primed for a bunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A couchette is a sleeping berth in a railway carriage, a bunk that folds down.

clue.text: Make early plans for speed ring, circuitous

indicators.note: circuitous means going round about, so the letters take a roundabout order

explanation.surface: Planning ahead for a speedway ring that winds round.
explanation.definitionFit: To predesign is to design or plan something beforehand, well in advance.

clue.text: Egg cell produced by ducks before due time in Scotland

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: a duck is a nought, O, so ducks are OO
tid is Scots for the proper time or mood

explanation.surface: An egg produced by ducks before the right time in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket, so ducks are two Os, placed before the Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ootid is an immature egg cell formed by meiosis before becoming a mature ovum.

clue.text: Biblical apparatus (a large number or one)

parts.note: a mass is a large quantity
a means one

explanation.surface: A parenthetical aside about a biblical device, one or many.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massora is the body of critical notes and traditions accompanying the Hebrew Bible text.

clue.text: Was frightened of consuming article only lightly touched

indicators.note: consuming something means taking it inside

parts.note: feared means was frightened of
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone afraid of eating an item, only nibbling it.
explanation.definitionFit: Feathered can mean brushed lightly, as an oar or paintbrush skims with a feather's touch.

clue.text: Historical land tax the Queen leaves to disperse

indicators.note: the Queen leaving means her letters go out of the word

parts.note: to scatter is to disperse
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A historic tax on land is abolished as the monarch departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatt was a tax paid on land in Orkney and Shetland, a historical levy.

clue.text: Little bird, young filly filled with energy and oomph (7, two words)

indicators.note: filled with means having something put inside

parts.note: a colt is a young horse
E is the physics symbol for energy
it means sex appeal, oomph

explanation.surface: A tiny bird and a lively young horse full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit, also spelt cole tit, is a small black-capped songbird of the tit family.

clue.text: Tantrum made public, ordered outside

indicators.note: the word for ordered goes outside the other piece

parts.note: bade means ordered, commanded
out means revealed, made public

explanation.surface: A fit of temper aired openly and ordered out.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutade is a sudden outburst or fit of temper, from French.

clue.text: Historian, chap confused with gen? Horror

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A muddled historian horrified by the information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles CHAP, GEN and HORROR together; gen is British slang for information, but here it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronographer is a chronicler, someone who records events in time order, an old word for a historian.

clue.text: Mingling of vowels, key moment when 'i' becomes 'a'

indicators.note: the clue spells out swapping an I for an A in the word

parts.note: a crisis is a crucial, decisive moment

explanation.surface: A grammar note about a crucial point when one vowel turns into another.
explanation.definitionFit: Crasis is the merging of two vowels into one long vowel or diphthong, in Greek grammar.

clue.text: Clergyman losing head in service offering advice on parenting

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a prelate is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A beheaded churchman working at a family counselling service.
explanation.walkthrough: PRELATE 'losing head' drops its P. Relate is a British charity giving relationship and family counselling.
explanation.definitionFit: Relate is the UK counselling organisation helping couples and families, including with parenting.

clue.text: Exercises outside, wind rising — woolly coat maybe needed

indicators.note: the exercises go outside, around the other piece

parts.note: PE is physical exercise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: Doing exercises outdoors in a rising wind calls for a woolly coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelage is the fur, hair or wool covering of a mammal, its natural coat.

clue.text: In a thin voice you'll need to rebuild with line not forte

indicators.note: line is L and forte is F in music, so L takes F's place

parts.note: to reedify is to rebuild

explanation.surface: Instructions for rebuilding with a line in place of a loud passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with line not forte' swaps the F (forte, the music mark for loud) of REEDIFY, an old word for rebuild, for L (line).
explanation.definitionFit: Reedily means in a high, thin tone, like the sound of a reed instrument.

clue.text: It's performed doloroso, dreadful when a bit of giocoso intervenes

indicators.note: something that intervenes comes in between, so it goes inside

parts.note: dire means dreadful

indicators.note: a bit of the word giocoso is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of giocoso

explanation.surface: A sorrowful piece ruined when a playful passage interrupts it.
explanation.walkthrough: Doloroso and giocoso are musical directions, sorrowful and playful; 'a bit of' gives the G of giocoso, which 'intervenes' in DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a lament or funeral song, naturally played in a sorrowful manner.

clue.text: Middle distance for Muscovite, run in singlet

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a vest is a singlet
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A Russian middle-distance athlete running in a vest.
explanation.definitionFit: A verst is an old Russian measure of distance, a little over a kilometre, middling in length.

clue.text: I must rise for senior churchman's reception — that's understood

indicators.note: the churchman's reception receives, so holds, the other piece

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: Someone must stand up for a bishop's reception, a point accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is radio slang for message received, meaning 'I understand'.

clue.text: In contact with uppish maid, was flirting

parts.note: to can mean touching, as in 'face to face'

indicators.note: uppish means turned upward, and in a down clue that reads the word backwards

parts.note: dey is an old Scots word for a dairymaid

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with a haughty maid while flirting.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with someone is to dally or trifle with them, flirtatiously.

clue.text: Tribal, yet roaming free (9, two words)

indicators.note: roaming means wandering, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Tribespeople still wandering at will.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at liberty means not confined or restrained, so able to act freely.

clue.text: District held by rebel troops

indicators.note: held by means contained within the following words

parts.note: the letters run on across the end of rebel and the start of troops

explanation.surface: A region occupied by insurgent forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is a zone or region, as in the commuter belt or corn belt.

clue.text: Miners' truck? It's for aligning machine parts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wagon in a coal mine
second meaning: ..., short for trammel, is a gauge for adjusting parts of a machine

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is short for trammel, an instrument used to set machine parts in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Tram covers both a colliery wagon on rails and an engineer's gauge for alignment.

clue.text: Religious teacher gets going about source of ecumenism

indicators.note: the word for gets going goes about, around, the other letter

parts.note: starts means gets going

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of ecumenism

explanation.surface: A cleric starts up a move toward church unity.
explanation.definitionFit: A starets is a Russian Orthodox elder, a spiritual adviser and teacher.

clue.text: Strange guys having regular trim of matted locks

indicators.note: trimming at regular intervals keeps every other letter of the words

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Odd blokes whose shaggy hair gets a regular cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like an anagram signal, but 'having regular trim' keeps every other letter of STRANGE GUYS, starting with the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Taggy is a Scots word describing hair or wool that is tangled and matted.

clue.text: Darwinian unit, information held in rectangular compartment

indicators.note: held in means placed inside

parts.note: a pane is a rectangular panel or section
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Data on a Darwinian unit kept in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin's pangenesis theory proposed pangenes, hypothetical heredity particles from every body part.

clue.text: We'll be accepted by group the misguided term 'deep' or 'benign'

indicators.note: being accepted by a group means going inside it

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clique welcoming us and labelling us either profound or kindly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet-tempered means having a gentle, kindly disposition, close to benign.
